title: Fast groove authoring
architecture: No design fork — story reuses the existing pointer-drag machinery in StepGrid.tsx (startBassDrag/extendBassDrag/endBassDrag/cellStepAtPoint) and the existing commitPatternEdit mutator path. StepGrid stays stateless/timerless; playhead from currentStep prop. No new deps.

tasks.story: As a composer, I want to drag across a drum row to paint/erase a run of steps, so I stop clicking each cell one at a time.
tasks.title: Add setDrum(p, pad, step, on) explicit on/off mutator to pattern.ts
constraints: Pure + immutable, mirror toggleDrum: fresh lane array, fresh drums record, inputs untouched.
A paint sweep needs explicit on/off, not a flip — toggleDrum flips and cannot be reused for the sweep.
Add assert coverage to the co-located _selfcheck (no test framework).
No new dependency.
tasks.acceptance: setDrum(p,'1',5,true).drums['1'][5]===true; setDrum on a lit cell with on=false clears it; input pattern unchanged (immutable); other lanes/steps untouched. _selfcheck asserts pass with no console.assert failures.
tasks.result: Added setDrum(p, pad, step, on): early-returns the same Pattern when the cell already matches (no needless re-render), else clones the lane like toggleDrum. Extended _selfcheck with on/off/no-op/immutability asserts.

tasks.story: As a composer, I want to drag across a drum row to paint/erase a run of steps, so I stop clicking each cell one at a time.
tasks.title: Generalize StepGrid pointer-drag to drums-mode paint; wire paint handler through usePattern
constraints: Generalize the existing bass-drag handlers to run in drums mode too (today gated `if (!bass) return`). Do NOT write a new drag system.
paintTarget = !filled of the first cell touched (start empty -> paint ON; start lit -> erase). Applies within the drag start row only (per-voice); no cross-row paint.
pointermove resolves cell via existing cellStepAtPoint; only commit when the step changes (mirror bassDragStep ref). Track paint row + last painted step.
Suppress the trailing onClick after a drag (generalize suppressBassClick -> suppressClick).
Single click still toggles one cell via existing onToggleCell.
StepGrid stays stateless/timerless; all edits flow through commitPatternEdit; no new deps.
tasks.acceptance: Press an empty kick step, drag right across 8 cells -> all 8 fill in one gesture; drag back over them -> all clear; single click on one cell still toggles just that cell; no stray extra toggle at drag end. Verified live in dev server + browser drag.
tasks.result: Generalized startBassDrag/extendBassDrag into mode-aware start/extend handlers: in drums mode pointerdown reads first-cell filled state, sets paintTarget=!filled, pins paint pad, applies via new onPaintDrum prop; pointermove paints each newly-entered cell in the same row only. suppressBassClick generalized to suppressClick. Added handlePaintDrum in usePattern (commitPatternEdit(setDrum) + audition on paint-on) and wired onPaintDrum in App.tsx. Verified in browser: 8-cell drag fills, reverse drag clears, single click toggles one, no stray end toggle.

tasks.story: As a composer, I want one-tap per-row fills (every 2/4/8, offbeat, backbeat, clear), so regular grooves need no manual clicking.
tasks.title: Add fillRow/clearRow pure helpers to pattern.ts
constraints: Pure + immutable, fresh lane/drums record.
fillRow REPLACES the row (clean pattern), not OR — acceptance says 'a clean four-on-the-floor'.

Layout is 8 steps/beat, 32 steps/bar (transport.ts loop = 8 beats at 32n). The EPIC doc's literal offsets (offbeat=every4 offset2, backbeat=every8 offset4) assume a 16-step/bar layout and are WRONG here; build to the acceptance contract instead.
Add asserts to co-located _selfcheck; no test framework.
tasks.acceptance: fillRow(p,pad,8) = one hit per beat across both bars ([0,8,16,24,32,40,48,56]); fillRow(p,pad,16,8) = backbeat on beats 2 & 4 ([8,24,40,56]); clearRow empties the row; all immutable.
tasks.result: Added fillRow(p,pad,everyN,offset=0) (replace semantics, proper modulo) and clearRow(p,pad). Corrected fill offsets for the real 8-steps/beat / 32-steps/bar layout: every8=four-on-the-floor, every16 offset8=backbeat (2&4), every8 offset4=offbeats. Extended _selfcheck with asserts for each. Selfcheck follows the house pattern (guarded off render path, not auto-invoked).

tasks.story: As a composer, I want one-tap per-row fills (every 2/4/8, offbeat, backbeat, clear), so regular grooves need no manual clicking.
tasks.title: Render per-row quick-fill chips on the StepGrid rail (drums only)
constraints: Chips on the .step-grid__rail row label, drums mode only (bass fills out of scope).
Each chip commits a pure helper via commitPatternEdit (threaded as onRowFill).

Fixed 118px rail can't hold 6 always-visible chips beside the long drum labels; used a native <details> disclosure (keyboard + touch accessible, no state code) with the menu absolutely positioned so opening it never reflows the rail or shifts the step-plane column centrelines.
Coarse-pointer (touch) gets larger chip/target sizes (AUDIT touch-first note).
No new deps.
tasks.acceptance: On the kick row, tap x8 -> clean four-on-the-floor across both bars; clr empties the row; backbeat on snare lands on 2 & 4; chips absent in bass mode. Verified live in browser.
tasks.result: Added a per-drum-row <details class=step-grid__fills> disclosure with chips x8/x4/x2/off/back/clr, each calling onRowFill((p)=>fillRow/clearRow(p,pad,...)). Threaded onRowFill = commitPatternEdit through App -> ScoreSection -> StepGrid. Fixed initial left-overflow by dropping the menu down from the rail's left edge (left:0, top:100%). Verified live: x8 kick=[0,8,16,24,32,40,48,56], snare backbeat=[8,24,40,56], clr empties kick to [], bass mode = 0 fill disclosures. tsc clean; no runtime console errors.

tasks.story: As a touch user, I want grid drags to paint instead of scrolling the page, so authoring works on a tablet at all.
tasks.title: Touch scroll-claim: touch-action:none on step cells + coarse-pointer single-tap target
constraints: CSS-only. No gesture library, no paint-mode toggle, no new deps.
touch-action:none goes on the paint surface (.step-cell), NOT a scroll container, so the rail and page outside the grid still scroll.
Existing Pointer Events + setPointerCapture (E1.1) then own the drag; no JS change needed.
Enlarge single-cell touch target via @media (pointer: coarse) without breaking the 64-column layout; horizontal enlargement is impossible at 64 cols, so grow row height only, or accept the limit.
tasks.acceptance: On coarse/touch, a finger-drag across a drum row paints a run and the page does not scroll; page scroll from outside the grid still works; single cell has a larger coarse-pointer hit area. Verified live.
tasks.result: Added touch-action:none to .step-cell (comment scopes it to the cell paint surface only, so rail + page-outside-grid keep scrolling; setPointerCapture drives the paint drag). Under @media (pointer: coarse), bumped --sg-row 24->36px on .step-grid — grows row height only (rail labels + plane rows both read --sg-row so they stay aligned), leaving the 64-column layout untouched since horizontal enlargement is impossible at 64 cols. Verified in browser: computed touch-action=none on .step-cell, coarse media rule '.step-grid{--sg-row:36px}' present in CSSOM; tsc clean, grid renders.
